question: Which of the following components is a part of a diesel engine only?
solution:
The correct answer is __Spray nozzle.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Spray nozzle__ is specifically used in diesel engines.
 
• Diesel engines do not use spark plugs or carburetors, which are components of petrol engines.
 
• The spray nozzle is responsible for atomizing the fuel for efficient combustion in diesel engines.
 
• Diesel engines operate using compression ignition, unlike petrol engines which use spark ignition.
 
• In this process, the spray nozzle ensures that fuel is injected into the combustion chamber in a fine mist, allowing for proper mixing with air.
 
• This fine mist of fuel is critical for achieving optimal combustion and efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Spark plug:**

 
 
• Used in petrol engines for ignition by generating a spark to ignite the air-fuel mixture.
 
• Not used in diesel engines as they rely on compression ignition.
 
 
 
• **Carburetor:**
 
 
• Used in older petrol engines to mix air and fuel before combustion.
 
• Diesel engines do not use a carburetor; instead, they use fuel injection systems.
 
 
 
• **Fuel tank:**
 
 
• Common to both diesel and petrol engines, stores fuel to be supplied to the engine.
